1. **Emulating a target trial of statin use and risk of dementia using cohort data.**
   Authors: Ellen C Caniglia, L Paloma Rojas-Saunero, Saima Hilal, Silvan Licher, Roger Logan, Bruno Stricker, M Arfan Ikram, Sonja A Swanson
   Journal: Neurology
   Publication Date: 2020-10-22
   PMID: 32753444
   PMC ID: 7538212 (Full text available)
   Abstract: Observational data can be used to attempt to emulate a target trial of statin use and estimate analogues of intention-to-treat and per protocol effects on dementia risk.
   **Full Text Available**
   Full Text (first 1000 chars): Correspondence Dr. Caniglia ellen.caniglia@nyulangone.org

Go to Neurology.org/N for full disclosures. Funding information and disclosures deemed relevant by the authors, if any, are provided at the end of the article.

Corresponding author.

Received 2019 Jun 29; Accepted 2020 Mar 16.

Observational data can be used to attempt to emulate a target trial of statin use and estimate analogues of intention-to-treat and per protocol effects on dementia risk.

Using data from a prospective cohort study in the Netherlands, we conceptualized a sequence of “trials” in which eligible individuals ages 55–80 years were classified as statin initiators or noninitiators for every consecutive month between 1993 and 2007 and were followed until diagnosis of dementia, death, loss to follow-up, or the end of follow-up. We estimated 2 types of effects of statin use on dementia and a combined endpoint of dementia or death: the effect of initiation vs no initiation and the effect of sustained use vs no use....
